A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same aggregation framework and research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original MATH and MATH500 experiments, aggregation accuracies, calibration sensitivity analyses, and estimation-error analyses in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original mathematical-reasoning experiments and adds multidomain evaluation, calibration-transfer tests, oracle-component ablations, self-verification experiments, and a pseudo-PRM simulation.

M1.justification: The KDE, linear, and logit calibration procedures and weighted-voting rules remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 evaluates the same aggregators using CISC confidence scores without specifying a new aggregation component or modified algorithm. The newly stated grid-search objective clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates mathematical reasoning on MATH and MATH500. V2 adds MMLU-Pro-CoT-Eval across 11 subjects, including health, law, history, philosophy, and engineering, together with cross-subject calibration-transfer scenarios in Sections 5.2–5.3.

E2.justification: The main Majority Vote, Best-of-N, and Vanilla Weighted Vote comparators remain. Appendix B.2 and Table 4 add two diagnostic comparators, KDE WV with an optimal PRM term and KDE WV with an optimal LLM term. The CISC experiment reuses the existing aggregation comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported MATH split from 1,000 calibration and 6,500 test questions to calibration sampling within a 2,000-question pool and 5,500 held-out test questions; MATH500 similarly changes from 100/400 to a 200-question pool and 300 test questions. New protocols include Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with VersaPRM at n=16, cross-subject testing, oracle-component controls, normalized weighting-function MSE, and synthetic verification scores.

E4.justification: V1 already analyzes weighting offsets, calibration-set size, question-specific weighting functions, and reliability-estimation error. V2 adds component-oracle ablations in Table 4, quantitative global-versus-question-specific function comparisons in Table 7, a controlled pseudo-PRM experiment in Table 8, and cross-domain calibration robustness in Table 3. These substantially expand the diagnosis of estimation failures and transferability.

E5.justification: V1's accuracy tables contain point values without a stated repeated-run count. V2 first specifies three runs with different seeds and adds ± quantities throughout Tables 1 and 5. This substantially changes uncertainty reporting, although the statistic represented by ± is undefined and the PDFs do not establish an increase from any particular previous run count.

E6.justification: MATH and MATH500 accuracy entries change, and substantial new results appear. For example, Table 1's Llama3.1-Mistral-8B averages change from 61.2 to 62.6 for Logit WV and from 58.2 to 59.4 for Vanilla WV; revised protocols prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains. New Table 2 reports multidomain averages of 58.8 versus 57.7, while Table 8 reports KDE WV at 57.1 versus Logit WV at 55.8 under synthetic scores.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the likelihood simplification from P(s_i|alpha_k,M), concerning the generated answer, to P(c_i|alpha_k,M), concerning binary correctness. Appendix A still uses s_i, leaving a localized mathematical inconsistency. The assumptions, optimal-weight theorem, and substantive proof otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: MAP-derived weighted aggregation, model-dependent negative weights, practical calibration, and improved test-time efficiency. The headline 37.1% and 21.3% computation claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning applicability beyond mathematics, cross-domain transfer, and self-verification signals. Appendix B strengthens the attribution of KDE's weakness to estimation difficulties and question-dependent score distributions. New Appendix C argues that calibration costs amortize after approximately 127 queries. The original limitations paragraph remains, including its now-outdated math-focused evaluation description.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly identifies held-out calibration accuracy as the grid-search objective. Appendix B specifies the P(True) implementation used for self-verification and normalization to (-0.5, 0.5) before weighting-function MSE calculation. These are limited additions to implementation and reproduction guidance.

R1.justification: Section 2's positioning is largely retained, but Appendix B.3 newly presents calibration as applicable to CISC's self-confidence signals. The additional Taubenfeld reference duplicates the already cited CISC work rather than introducing a distinct paper; the substantive change is the newly articulated relationship.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the six-section main narrative remain intact. V2 adds localized experimental discussion, Appendix B subsections, a calibration-cost appendix, and acknowledgments, alongside conference-header and wording edits. The original limitations appendix moves from C to D without substantive rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 adds substantial table displays for multidomain evaluation, transfer, oracle ablations, self-verification, function discrepancy, and synthetic scores. Existing benchmark tables incorporate ± entries, and v1's MATH500 Table 2 becomes Table 5. Conference formatting changes typography, headers, spacing, and placement throughout; the four existing figures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's narrow empirical scope and limited controlled diagnosis through multidomain and transfer tests, oracle-component ablations, and the pseudo-PRM experiment. Three-seed reporting also improves assessment of calibration stability. These gains outweigh localized reporting problems, including undefined ± quantities, outdated limitations wording, and Section 5.2 retaining the 61.2/58.2 example although Table 1 now reports 62.6/59.4.
